SMTO-CTR-0006 — An attached file changed after you sent the request

GUID: 068a83a3-5abe-4110-8ded-297b70706e29
Slug: task-contract-context-revision-changed
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • SMTO recorded the exact contents of each attached file when you sent the request. One file's contents are now different, so SMTO didn't act on this version of your request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the attached file and decide whether SMTO should use its new contents or the original ones. SMTO won't guess which version you meant, because the plan was based on the original contents.
  2. Send the request again as a new message and attach the version you want with Add context. A new request records that version's contents, so the plan and the file match.
  3. Don't keep selecting Retry on the old task. Retry still expects the original contents, so it stops at the same check.

What success looks like

  • The new task shows Task contract generated and starts working with the version you attached.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep retrying the old task; it will stop at the same check each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Task Contract context source's current SHA-256 differs from the hash captured in the run's context manifest, so its content changed after capture.

What this means

  • available_context compares the current context SHA-256 with the captured manifest hash and detects changed content. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • available_context compares the current context SHA-256 with the captured manifest hash and detects changed content.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact context ID and captured/current revision before choosing which source is intended.

How to fix it

  • available_context found that the current SHA-256 of a captured context source differs from the hash stored in available_context_manifest. Review the changed source, then start a new request so a fresh capture and compilation use the intended current content, instead of retrying with the stale manifest.
  • Review the changed source and compile against its intended current revision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported new capture and compilation use the explicitly intended current content.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
